\begin{tablenotes}\notesize
\item Notes: The coefficient is the three-year first difference of Eq.~(\ref{eq:group}) of the paper for the log count of young workers, 2026Q1 vs.\ 2023Q1 and 2026Q2 vs.\ 2023Q2 stacked, with the twelve base-period composition controls, base-period young employment weights, and standard errors clustered by occupation, i.e., the under-30 row of Table~\ref{tab:cell_fd_main_4} of the paper and the young non-graduate cell of Table~\ref{tab:cell_fd_main_5}, decomposed in Figures~\ref{fig:decomposition} and~\ref{fig:decompgroups} of the paper. After the controls and the period effect are partialled out, the coefficient equals the weighted sum over occupations of the product of the exposure-change deviation and the outcome deviation, divided by the weighted sum of squared exposure-change deviations, and each occupation's term is its contribution. Rows sum the contributions within the 22 major census occupation groups. A negative contribution comes from occupations with above-average exposure change whose young employment fell relative to prediction, or from occupations with below-average exposure change whose young employment rose relative to prediction. Mean exposure change is the unweighted mean of the stage-1 to stage-4 change across the group's occupations; share of young employment is the group's share of the base-period weights.
\end{tablenotes}
